headline: High-risk data leakage and cascading-error pathways exist because Perplexity ingests uploaded content and browser context while godot_rl_agents has no documented isolation or output controls.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A direct injection bridge is not documented: godot_rl_agents shows no I/O surfaces, while Perplexity uses browser/search tools and uploaded files. The only plausible pathway is manual copy-paste or user-mediated transfer into Perplexity, so the blast radius is limited. Uncertainty about hidden integrations pushes this above none.
conditions: IF the operator manually pastes godot_rl_agents output into Perplexity prompts
IF Perplexity is asked to follow instructions embedded in uploaded files or web pages
mitigations: Avoid pasting raw agent output into Perplexity
Strip instructions from any uploaded documents
Use a fixed prompt template that ignores quoted content
Review Perplexity answers before reusing them
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between tools

B_data_leakage.rationale: Perplexity explicitly handles uploaded documents and browsing context, so any sensitive material placed there can flow to its vendor-hosted backend. godot_rl_agents has no documented data classes touched, but the pair still creates a default leakage path if the operator moves artifacts from A into B. The shared-workspace risk is indirect, so medium fits.
conditions: IF outputs from godot_rl_agents are uploaded to Perplexity
IF uploaded documents contain secrets, credentials, or private data
mitigations: Do not upload sensitive artifacts to Perplexity
Redact secrets before analysis
Use synthetic samples for testing
Limit Perplexity queries to non-sensitive summaries
requires-engineering: enforce DLP on uploads

C_capability_conflict.rationale: godot_rl_agents has no documented write, network, or git mutation surfaces, while Perplexity cannot write files, modify git state, or execute shell commands. That makes direct resource conflict unlikely. The only overlap is read/analysis of user-provided content, so the conflict blast radius is small.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator grants both agents write access outside the documented profiles
IF the operator manually synchronizes mutable files between them
mitigations: Keep both agents read-only in the same workflow
Do not share writable directories
Avoid concurrent edits to the same artifact
Use separate workspaces
requires-engineering: add locking around shared resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: Perplexity is a search-RAG answer engine that can render cited answers from browsing context, while godot_rl_agents is a game-playing project with no documented verification layer. If A's generated content is fed into B as authoritative context, B may present it as grounded output without independent validation. The pathway exists in default usage when users chain them.
conditions: IF godot_rl_agents output is used as source material for Perplexity answers
IF Perplexity is instructed to trust prior-agent output without verification
mitigations: Require source checking before reuse
Ask Perplexity to cite primary sources only
Separate generation from verification steps
Flag A-originated claims as untrusted
requires-engineering: add automated fact-validation

E_compliance.rationale: No PHI, residency, or retention mismatch is documented for godot_rl_agents, and Perplexity's docs only show vendor-hosted processing of search queries, uploaded documents, and browsing context. Because the pair lacks a specific regulated-data class, compliance risk is limited to ordinary policy mismatch if the operator introduces sensitive data. The other agent is not cited beyond its lack of touched data classes.
conditions: IF regulated data is uploaded to Perplexity
IF organizational policy forbids vendor-hosted processing of browsing context
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of Perplexity
Check internal data-handling policy first
Use anonymized excerpts only
Document retention expectations
requires-engineering: obtain a DPA or approved deployment
